newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bankinter eases with market after 96 profit. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bankinter eases with market after 96 profit. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Spain's Bankinter eased in line with the market on Tuesday after the release of 1996 results which broadly met forecasts, analysts and dealers said.
At 1055 GMT, Bankinter was down 80 pesetas, or 0.40 percent, to 19,820, off a low of 19,700. The Ibex index of leading stocks was off 54.75 points, or 1.0 percent, to 5,435.68.
The stock was expected to trade in line with the market during the rest of the session, dealers said.
Bankinter this morning announced a rise in 1996 net profit to 17.14 billion pesetas from 15.29 billion pesetas in the previous year.
Analysts said the bank seemed to be revealing less profits at the net level after a good year, aiming to report steady results growth in years to come which may not be so fruitful.

"Basically they're hiding profits all over the shop. They've reported much smaller profits from financial operations than they needed to, and although I haven't seen the provisions for non-performing loans they're probably provisioning more," said Miguel Olabarri, banks analyst at Credit Lyonnais Securities.
"The idea is to keep the outlook at 10-15 percent (annual) growth," he added.
Bankinter managing director (Corrects from chairman) Juan Arena said at a news conference today that pre-tax profit could rise 10 percent in 1997.
Analysts had forecast on average a rise in 1996 results to 17.39 billion pesetas, according to a Reuter poll.
